title: RAW: full f83r P3 work-period summary paired with P4 under all 24 unchanged unweaving meanings
summary: Unreviewed exploratory extension of RAW404 to the complete already-owned 63-group f83r.18–24 paragraph, retaining all 33 old groups and all 24 old denotations. Seven old types occupy 17 new positions; 40 explicitly new whole-word values occupy 46. Eleven new clause shapes and seven additional binding conventions are declared. This is a conditional full draft, not a tested translation or source identification.

decision_note.unknown: Can the two complete fixed paragraphs share the old word denotations, cloth, worker, action pair, earlier period and compelled completion without a type error or temporal contradiction? The new content is allowed to be guessed. This proposal does not require a newly confirmed word and does not claim absence of later tests.
decision_note.smallest_decision_changing_check: If selected by root, inspect all 96 assignments and derive the two complete typed assertion graphs before imposing the seven declared joint bindings. Check the unchanged original and the already owned reversed RESPECTIVELY schedule fork. FIRST must return an activity type, FINISHED must remain the predicate of the same C, a required/nominal predicate must not execute, and the two completion descriptions must denote one Z. Stop on an original contradiction; retain no repair of words, boundaries or aliases. No new interpreter is proposed here.
decision_note.outcomes: An incoherent original rejects this joint descendant only. A coherent original with incompatible reverse schedule narrows only this explicitly augmented conditional model, not manuscript meaning. If both schedules remain compatible, the new binding has not separated them. No outcome confirms any of the 64 word values or reopens a reserve.
decision_note.producer_budget: At most25min including documentation and ideas add; started about2026-09-21 04:43UTC, finish by05:08UTC. No model test run.
decision_note.prospective_selected_budget: Root chooses independently; at most45min for a bounded whole-graph audit using existing means, including validation/publication, before any separate decoder decision.

source.owned: Homer Odyssey II.93–110 within Antinous's hostile speech, Murray translation; the existing receipt and RAW404 source review only, no new source fetch.
source.source_attested: Daytime weaving, nocturnal undoing, torches as preserved in RAW404's inspected source account, delayed finishing, discovery and forced completion. No equal nightly undoing, exact daily quantity, or executed marriage.
source.new_elaboration: The public participants judging from daytime appearances, their explicit demand construction, an ordered nominal summary, explicit every-day recurrence and the exact progress-before-completion assertion are this descendant's narrative elaborations. They are not verbatim translated source clauses. N3 knowledge absence is compatible with the source concealment but the explicit epistemic operator and its wording are invented.
source.omissions_preserved: This is still not a full translation of the bounded Homer episode: Laertes, three/four years, anticipated death, wasted spinning, reproach, hostile narrator ownership and the entire quoted explanation are not encoded. Parent's row-by-row and daytime-pledge assumptions remain. The source channel to this manuscript is unidentified.
source.no_new_historical_claim: The extra paragraph summarizes and comments on the same episode; that literary organization is itself an assumption.

target.P12_projection_difference: The seven projected P3 lines match the selected ZL3b record's word strings, but f83r.21 has anchor_eligible=false. That flag is preserved; matching strings do not repair its uncertainty.

all_nine_grammar_rows.rule: Literal whole forms and typed constructions only. Inherited action names are not occurrence counts: C1 has two action names, C3 one habitual unweaving assertion, C5 one habitual weaving assertion, C8 one bounded weaving assertion. No character, suffix or segment meaning is inferred.

ACTION contrast ACTION OBJECT constructs an ordered pair of action types sharing its following object. It does not execute either action. STATE SOCIAL_ACT constructs a prospective prerequisite proposition. These two constructions are nominal/propositional contexts; bare action clauses elsewhere assert the written action.

There is one persistent cloth C. Its first literal qokedy introduces C; later qokedy refers to C. Inherited weave/unravel/finish predicates have C as patient by their unchanged meanings. A written worker noun binds the worker; subsequent omitted worker arguments use the most recent compatible worker. W first appears in C3, before every actor-requiring asserted clause. C2 is initially an open proposition and receives W when PLEDGE binds it; no forward invisible person or action is inserted.

Modifiers precede their action head, except a postposed actor and an action-final completive. TIME preceding a speech predicate attaches to that speech act. UNTIL STATE ACTION marks a prospective endpoint and does not assert its achievement. ACTION ROW ROW uses the explicitly hypothetical distributive noun repetition construction. It has no number, duration, recurrence count or extra action semantics.

PLEDGE selects the most recent prerequisite proposition. A public/secret modifier shares the participant class PublicParticipants, explicitly named as wooers in C7. Until that noun is read, O is an unfilled participant slot, not an invented independent agent. Completion predicates in C2 and C5 and the endpoint in C8 all apply to C.

FIRST SECOND RESPECTIVELY OBJECT TIME1 TIME2 assigns times to the most recent asserted habitual actions of the two ordered types with that same object. The pair is C1, actions are C5 and C3, object is C, times are DAY and NIGHT. All required frames must already exist; failure to find either is an error, not permission to add an event. This clause makes no new action.

PERSON INFORM PERSON DISCOVER TIME is a serial construction: the second person is recipient of INFORM and subject of DISCOVER; the final time modifies DISCOVER only. Both predicates take the most recent concealed-action frame as content. No additional UNRAVEL is generated by either predicate.

The passage has descriptive habitual clauses and one later discovery/completion sequence. C3 and C5 describe the same prior work period; their textual order does not impose alternating executions. C7 introduces discovery of that period; THEN in C8 explicitly advances after it. No exact cycle count, no equal daily/nightly amount, no silent reset, no inferred executed marriage.

Clause boundaries are the explicit hypothesized eight spans, justified only conditionally by these construction signatures. They are not observed historical punctuation. This is a fully specified interpretive reading, not a demonstrated uniquely recoverable parser, and the rule list has not been fit or tested elsewhere.

seven_new_binding_conventions.rule: Joint identity is a new explicit assumption: P3 and unchanged P4 describe the same C, W, O and episode. Their nominal pairs have the same ordered values [WEAVE,UNRAVEL]. Keep every P4 construction, asserted event and predicate unchanged, then require the named cross-paragraph identities. Parent references to its first introductions remain descriptions of its standalone scope, not instructions to create a second physical cloth or worker. FIRST keeps its literal most-recent-pair rule in full written order: at .20 it selects N1's A3, and at .28 it selects the intervening parent C1 pair, with identical ordered type values.

P3 E is exactly the earlier habitual work period already used by P4 C3/C5. P3 habitual V3=parent V, nominal U type=parent concealed U type, and P3 compelled Z3=parent C8 Z. These two frame identities plus one action-type identity are additional hypotheses, not obtained from identical action names alone. P3 does not add an actual U event. P4's explicit discovery ordering gives E before discovery before Z. No textual paragraph ordering makes P4 a later second episode.

WHEN has one temporal-condition operation over a declared two-case input type: a TimeRegion yields its membership predicate on t; a StatePredicate such as FINISHED(C) yields truth of that same predicate in the state at t. ONSET takes the first attainment boundary of the resulting condition in this episode. No new patient argument is substituted into FINISHED, and no word meaning is replaced by a generic predicate label.

The SAME_PATIENT/WORK_PATIENT_ROLE construction introduces one unresolved artifact variable, not a second artifact. N4's first literal qokedy must bind it to C before the completed assertions of N2/N3 are accepted. This prospective reference over N1–N4 is new grammar and a cost; failure to bind rejects the draft. N5 supplies W before applying FIRST; no invisible early actor is added.

Each P3 DAY qualification on WEAVE in N1 is a sole day/night phase value for the habitual frame V in E, not merely permission to weave on some days. DAY and NIGHT are disjoint alternatives in that schedule field. This exclusivity is a new narrow assumption of P1, not entailed by the English word daytime or by old RAW404 alone. It is the additional condition needed for the already owned reverse-schedule fork to conflict with P3 after B2.

State assertions and knowledge absence in N2/N3/N6/N9 are scoped to E; N8 attains FINISHED(C) in Z; N10 ONSET refers to that same outcome. Requirements and nominal activity specifications remain unexecuted. N10's progress occurrences are realizations of V in E; N11's recurrence concerns those occurrences, not additional action types or another weaving event after Z.

P3 phrase and clause boundaries are the eleven enumerated spans, not observed punctuation. CONCERNING always constructs a typed topic (artifact or complete activity specification); IN_CONTRAST always relates adjacent complete discourse items; otaiin always names E; sar always O. No singleton escape meaning or paragraph-specific dictionary is permitted.
